An explorable is an interactive web simulation of a model. You can change parameters and initial conditions and watch the dynamics respond. In Sessions 27 and 28 you present one explorable to the class, together with a partner.

A large collection is available at [Complexity Explorables](https://www.complexity-explorables.org).

## Format

- You work in **pairs**.
- Each pair presents for **ten minutes**.
- **Five pairs** present in each session.
- You choose your model **one to two weeks in advance**.
- The presentation is worth **10% of the final grade**.

<!-- TODO(Daniel): confirm how pairs register their model choice (form, Blackboard, email) and the exact deadline. -->

## What your presentation must do

Your ten minutes must cover three things:

1. **Explain what is modelled.** Say which real system the explorable represents and which quantities the model tracks.
2. **State the assumptions.** List the simplifications behind the rules or equations.
3. **Add something of your own.** This can be an extension of the model, a test of its behaviour, or a criticism of its assumptions.

## Why this matters for your project

The explorables also guide the choice of your final group project. The models you and your classmates present give you a list of candidate systems to build on. See the project pages in Module 7 when you start choosing a topic.
